Isla de Lobos
candidates.reason: Both passes independently surfaced this as the marquee boat excursion; Pass B declined to deep-verify it separately, recognizing it as the mainstream pick Pass A already owns rather than a novel local find.

candidates.name: Cabo Polonio
candidates.reason: A genuinely wild, un-electrified sea-lion coast and dune settlement — the strongest single nature find for this trip — but reaching it costs a full day round trip from Punta del Este (road plus a 4x4 dune transfer each way). Presented as an opt-in detour on the one open day rather than fixed into a 9-day, 3-city itinerary that already has fixed logistics on both sides. A commercially-sold day-trip tour product from Punta del Este confirms same-day feasibility (see disagreement d-cabo-polonio-feasibility).

candidates.reason: Resident-frequented, better-value indoor market alternative to Mercado del Puerto per one fresh (2026) firsthand travel-blog account. A second account corroborates but dates to 2021, past the 24-month experiential-freshness bar, so it stays shortlisted rather than shipped — the objective hours/address are T0-verified, but the 'calmer, less touristy' framing lacks a second current independent source. Lo de Silverio (shipped) already fills the 'novel local food pick' role this trip; this stays a recorded lead for a future pass.

candidates.name: José Ignacio
candidates.reason: Quieter, more upscale beach town roughly 30-40 minutes from central Punta del Este. Positioned as a day-trip pairing with the traveler's stated interest in the Punta del Este beach scene, not a replacement for it; woven into the Fri Feb 12 beach-day text.

candidates.name: La Pedrera
candidates.reason: Mentioned as a cheaper, calmer beach-town alternative further from the trip's three named cities. Only one source found (Ohlalá!, Feb 2025) and not independently corroborated — flagged as a lead, not shipped.

candidates.name: Laguna Garzón
candidates.reason: Protected-area lagoon with kayak/SUP/birdwatching tours run by a certified local operator, past José Ignacio on the coastal road toward Rocha; fits the nature/outdoors priority as a lighter-commitment day trip than Cabo Polonio. T0-verified via the operator's own site (activities, booking channel); no fixed schedule or price, booking is by WhatsApp with limited capacity. Woven into the Fri Feb 12 open day.

evidence.claim: Uruguay's Carnival public holidays (Lunes y Martes de Carnaval) fall Feb 8–9, 2027 — computed Easter-relative (48/47 days before Easter Sunday, which is Mar 28, 2027), not separately announced each year

The Desfile de Llamadas parade's most recent officially-confirmed dates are Friday Feb 6 and Saturday Feb 7, 2026 (Isla de Flores, Montevideo); the 2027 dates had not been posted on the event's official page as of this check
US citizens traveling on a regular (non-diplomatic) passport do not need a visa for tourism and are granted 90 days on arrival
CDC recommends hepatitis A and B (plus routine vaccines) for most travelers to Uruguay; yellow fever is not recommended

travel.state.gov is Cloudflare-gated against automated fetch (403) in this environment; a search synthesis (via the US Embassy Montevideo's own renewal notice) suggests Level 2 as of a July 2026 renewal, but this is a lead, not a fetched primary verification
COT bus Montevideo (Tres Cruces) → Colonia del Sacramento: UYU 579 one-way, ≈2h20m, frequent departures from 05:00
COT bus Montevideo (Tres Cruces) → Punta del Este: UYU 466 one-way, ≈2h, frequent departures from 04:45

Carrasco Airport → downtown Montevideo: official taxi desk exists with a fare calculator (fixed-fare structure), or public buses to Tres Cruces/downtown — exact bus line numbers and precise minutes are a cross-checked lead, not independently fetched
No nonstop flight exists between JFK and Montevideo (MVD) as of this check; every routing connects (commonly via São Paulo, Panama City, or Bogotá)
Faro de Colonia (lighthouse) is open Thursday–Sunday 10:00–12:00 and 15:00–17:00, UYU 35 entrance, minimum age 8, closed-toe shoes required
Casapueblo is open daily from 10:00; admission UYU 600 (adult), UYU 500 (65+), free under 12
Museo del Carnaval is open Wednesday–Sunday 11:00–17:00 (closed Mon/Tue), UYU 200 admission, free under 12; keeps regular hours during Carnival week itself
Isla de Lobos boat excursion departs daily at 12:00, ≈2h round trip, US$70 adult / US$50 child under 10; no landing permitted on the island itself
Palacio Salvo guided tours are booked exclusively through Red Ticket (redtickets.uy) — confirmed by a live listed event (Aug 24, 2026, 10:30, Spanish, with further times shown) — no door sales exist

Montevideo Municipio B's own page still lists a different, likely-outdated tour arrangement (Tue/Thu/Sat 15:00/16:00/17:00, UYU 200, phone/Facebook booking) that conflicts with Red Ticket's current listings

Mercado del Puerto was inaugurated Oct 10, 1868; the building keeps Mon–Sat 9:00–17:00, Sun 10:00–17:00 hours (exterior bars later), with Sunday the busiest day and 11:30–15:00 the market's own recommended window
El Palenque (Mercado del Puerto) hours: Tue–Fri 12:00–23:00, Sat–Sun 12:00–17:00, closed Mondays
El Palenque addresses: Pérez Castellano 1579 (Montevideo, Mercado del Puerto); Parada 7, Av. Roosevelt (Punta del Este)
Bodega Bouza is located at Cno. de la Redención 7658 bis, Melilla (greater Montevideo), phone +598 2323 4030
Antel's official prepaid "Chip Prepago" SIM costs $65 UYU, requiring a minimum top-up of $220 to activate service
Mid-market exchange rate: 1 USD ≈ 40.1496 UYU
Restaurant tipping (propina) of ≈10% is customary but not legally required; the "cubierto" cover charge is a separate house fee (bread/setting), not a tip

Cabo Polonio's sea lion reserve (two coexisting species, males to 340 kg) sits on rocks near the Cabo Polonio Lighthouse, inside Parque Nacional Cabo Polonio, with breeding-season colonies described as extremely loud in summer

No regular paved-road vehicle access reaches Cabo Polonio's settlement itself — the last stretch is by 4x4 across dunes — a durable, long-standing access arrangement rather than a recently-changed one, effectively consuming a full day round trip from Punta del Este
Uruguay's Carnival is widely described as the longest in the world, running roughly 40 days from mid/late January
Uruguay's Ministry of Tourism runs a free non-emergency tourist helpline (0800-8748, business hours); seasonal tourist police patrol Ciudad Vieja (Montevideo) and Colonia's historic quarter in summer

Buenos Aires day-tripper ferries land and depart Colonia between roughly 10:00 and 15:00; arriving before 10:00 or staying past 16:00 shows a visibly quieter, more photogenic old town once the day-trip crowd has left.

Colonia's historic quarter gets 'MUITO mais mágica' (much more magical) in the late afternoon and evening, once the same-day ferry tourists ('bate-volta') have already left; the author frames overnighting there as the way to see the town at its best.
The 08:30 Buenos Aires-Colonia ferry departure is the most crowded of the day; the author recommends a mid-morning sailing instead. Single-sourced within this pass, not independently corroborated.
Mercado Agrícola de Montevideo (MAM) is open daily 09:00-22:00 overall, with the gastronomy section 11:00-23:00 and shops 10:00-22:00, at José L. Terra 2220.

MAM is 'mais moderno, mistura gastronomia com mercado de verdade. Frequentado por moradores locais' — attracts local residents, in contrast to Mercado del Puerto, which the same author calls 'mais antigo, mais turístico.' Weekdays Tue-Fri are quieter than Saturdays.

MAM is 'another good option in the city and is less touristic' than Mercado del Puerto, and 'a more complete market' with broader food/shop offerings. Published Sept 2021 — outside the 24-month experiential-freshness window, recorded as a re-verify lead rather than current corroboration.
Lo de Silverio (Alejo Rossell y Rius 1655 esquina 4 de Julio, Villa Dolores) is open Tuesday-Saturday 12:00-16:00 and 20:00-00:00, Sunday 12:00-16:00.

José Ignacio stays 'discreto, lindo y curado' in February — busy but noticeably less intense than January's peak; recommended for long lunches and a quieter register than central Punta, best visited as a day trip while staying in Punta (Mansa or the Península) for practicality.

'Las playas de José Ignacio son menos concurridas, ofreciendo un entorno más sereno' compared to Punta del Este's nightlife-driven, crowd-seeking scene — José Ignacio draws travelers wanting privacy and calm rather than the multitudes.
La Pedrera has 'more middle-class presence,' is 'más gasoleras' (less flashy) than Punta del Este, and its lack of large nightclubs keeps a calmer, safer atmosphere. Single-sourced within this pass.

Laguna Garzón's local operator runs kayak, SUP, and canoe outings on the lagoon plus guided birdwatching, forest-bathing walks, and astronomy sessions; booking is by WhatsApp/contact form with 'cupos limitados' (limited capacity) and no fixed public schedule beyond checking the next available date.

Uruguayan Spanish uses voseo ('vos' + 'tenés'/'sos' conjugations, not 'tú'). Everyday words a first-time visitor will hear: botija/gurí (kid), championes (sneakers), bondi (bus), buzo (sweater), tá (filler, short for 'está'), al mango (full-on/maxed out), de más (excellent — positive, unlike standard Spanish usage).

reservations.walkIn: Not walk-in — the operator requires advance booking via WhatsApp/contact form due to limited capacity per outing and does not publish a fixed daily schedule ('consultá la próxima fecha').
reservations.alternatives: Turismo Rocha (turismorocha.gub.uy) lists the same protected-area activities under the government tourism portal for the department, as an alternative discovery/contact route if the operator's own channel is unresponsive — not independently fetched this pass.

reservations.walkIn: Not explicitly confirmed on the official site; phone (+598 2628 4771) and email are listed for contact but no stated walk-in policy — calling ahead is advisable for dinner-service hours (20:00-00:00) given ~100-guest capacity and live-music nights.

disagreements.topic: Palacio Salvo guided-tour day/time grid and booking channel
disagreements.investigation: Montevideo's own Municipio B page (fetched) states Tue/Thu/Sat 15:00–17:00 tours booked by phone/Facebook at UYU 200. Multiple independent tour aggregators (GetYourGuide, descubrimontevideo.uy, Trip.com) converge on a different, more granular grid — Mon–Fri 10:30/12:00/14:00/16:30 (ES) plus English times, Sat 10:00/10:30/12:00, Sun 12:00/14:00 — booked exclusively through Red Ticket, no door sales. Fetching Red Ticket's own event listing directly confirmed an active, currently-selling event (Aug 24, 2026, 10:30, Spanish, with more times available), which corroborates the Red-Ticket-based system as the CURRENT one and the Municipio B page as stale content still live on a government domain.
disagreements.resolution: Shipped the Red-Ticket/aggregator-converged schedule as the operative one, but softened the guide's specific day-time claims to a range with an explicit ⚠ inviting confirmation at booking, since no single fetch produced the complete official grid — only the booking CHANNEL (Red Ticket, no door sales) is fetched-solid.

disagreements.topic: '90 days' vs '90 business days' for the US tourist stay allowance
disagreements.investigation: The Uruguay embassy's own tourism-visa page uses '90 días hábiles' (business days); several tourism aggregators simplify this to a flat 90 calendar days. For a 9-day trip the distinction is immaterial either way.
disagreements.resolution: Guide states '90 days' without over-specifying business vs. calendar, since it doesn't change this trip's planning and over-precision here risks asserting a distinction the sources themselves don't agree on.

disagreements.topic: Whether Cabo Polonio is reachable as a single-day round trip from Punta del Este, or effectively requires an overnight stay
disagreements.investigation: Pass A cited a commercially-sold day-trip tour product from Punta del Este (civitatis.com, 'Cabo Polonio day trip') as evidence the round trip is a feasible single day (road plus a 4x4 dune transfer, consuming the whole day). Pass B's candidate table called it 'requiring an overnight detour outside this trip's shape' but cited no source for that claim — it was Pass B's own reasoning for treating the destination as out of scope, not a sourced contradiction of Pass A's fetched-tour-product evidence.
disagreements.resolution: Kept the existing guide framing (an optional, full-day round trip from Punta del Este, not fixed into the itinerary) — Pass A's citation of an actual commercial day-trip product outweighs Pass B's uncited assumption. Both passes agree it should stay an opt-in detour rather than a fixed stop, so the practical guide outcome is unchanged either way.

reservations.notApplicableReason: No shipped or detour candidate in this run is a scarce-release booking (no ticketed anchor with a release window, no reservation-only restaurant): El Palenque and the sights are walk-in or simple same-week online tickets; Bodega Bouza, Isla de Lobos, Lo de Silverio, and Laguna Garzón are advance-contactable but not scarcity-constrained. Casual-importance reservation notes for Lo de Silverio and Laguna Garzón are recorded in reservations[] for completeness, not because either clears the required-depth bar.

transport.notApplicableReason: The only intercity legs are the Montevideo–Colonia and Montevideo–Punta del Este COT bus routes, both high-frequency (departures roughly hourly), well under R3 risk — a missed departure has a same-day next-bus fallback, not a stranding consequence. The Buenos Aires–Colonia ferry crowd-timing factor Pass B researched affects sightseeing crowds, not this itinerary's own transport legs (the travelers arrive from Montevideo by bus, not from Buenos Aires by ferry). No route in this itinerary reaches R3+.

saturation.note: Both passes independently reached the same stopping point. Pass A: later searches on Montevideo parrillas, Punta del Este beach sights, and Colonia old-town attractions mostly re-surfaced the same handful of names (El Palenque, Mercado del Puerto stalls, Casapueblo, La Mano) across different aggregators, with no new serious contender emerging. Pass B: a final search round (Isla de Lobos boat tours, traditional Sunday-asado timing) returned mainstream press coverage already surfaced or generic cultural background with no new resident-angle specifics; several native-language aggregator leads (Don Beto, La Otra Parrilla, Pellicer, Asados Iruña, La Pedrera, the 08:30-ferry-crowding detail) remain single- or zero-sourced and are recorded as rejected/considered/shortlisted rather than pushed further. The one open item across both passes — the Desfile de Llamadas' exact 2027 dates — is unresolved but does not change any recommendation: the Carnival-season framing, the two legal holiday days, and every shipped venue/detour pick hold regardless of which exact nights the parade itself lands on.

nativeLanguage.why: Uruguay's resident/blog layer writes in Spanish, plus a large body of firsthand Brazilian Portuguese travel blogging aimed at the huge Argentine/Brazilian day-tripper audience that dominates Colonia and Punta del Este. English top-10 sources are Pass A's territory and under-sample local crowd-timing tactics and off-default food/nature picks.
